source.title: Calibrating the Learning Rate for Adaptive Gradient Methods to Improve Generalization Performance
source.authors: Qianqian Tong; Guannan Liang; J. Bi

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers and momentum on held-out performance using its own experiments, with a different optimizer set and benchmark protocol from the version’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper’s own optimizer comparisons on image-classification benchmarks. The cited prior claims about Adam’s generalization gap are not rows. A-LR range observations do not measure the sharpness–generalization relationship in V7. Language-model results are described in figures without extractable values or method-specific text results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam, AMSGrad and momentum comparisons on held-out image accuracy. These bear on V4, although tuning includes momentum parameters and algorithm-specific parameters, exceeding V4's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that softplus calibration improves Adam and AMSGrad generalization across their tested tasks and can outperform momentum. They also present convergence bounds depending on epsilon or beta. Their claim that Sadam is best among competitors is not universal: SAMSGrad is higher on some architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a proposed softplus calibration of Adam and AMSGrad and grid-searches base learning rate and optimizer parameters; compares the resulting methods with S-Momentum and other adaptive optimizers.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, architecture, dataset, and training epoch change the relative test accuracy; the paper also says beta can be fine-tuned for better accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Sadam and SAMSGrad improve held-out performance through a proposed softplus calibration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Softplus calibration of adaptive learning rates can improve Adam-family optimizer performance on the tested workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive learning-rate coordinates span a large range, which softplus calibration reduces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Calibrating adaptive learning rates reduces their coordinate-wise dispersion; this is not a measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness.

record.problems: The paper reports means and standard deviations for repeated CIFAR experiments but does not state the number of repetitions for CIFAR-100 tables in the supplied text. Test-accuracy results for PTB and WT2 appear only as figure curves and lack extractable method-specific values here. No direct training-versus-test error gap is reported for the main optimizer comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the extractable numeric image-classification comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix Tables 2–3. PTB and WT2 method-specific figure results (Figures 6 and related curves) are not transcribed as rows because the supplied text gives no values or textual optimizer-specific outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

A protocol tuning only learning rates and decay schedules; controlled limited-versus-broader tuning comparisons; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD. The supplied language-model text does not resolve original Adam versus momentum. The numeric rows do not establish equal or better training performance.
Batch-size comparisons and recipes for removing a large-batch penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: The study's own CIFAR-10 S-Momentum comparator rows: 92.73 ± 0.05, 94.11 ± 0.15 and 95.03 ± 0.15 for ResNet20, ResNet56 and DenseNet.

Original AMSGrad results: CIFAR-10 accuracies 91.70 ± 0.12, 93.10 ± 0.11 and 93.71 ± 0.05. CIFAR-100 VGGNet epoch-250/best accuracies are 74.04 ± 0.16/74.26 ± 0.18; ResNet18 values are 75.92 ± 0.26/76.32 ± 0.11. Early checkpoints also exceed momentum in mean accuracy.
missing.locator: Table 1 and Appendix Tables 2–3, AMSGrad rows

missing.what: Additional adaptive baselines were omitted despite the record's completeness statement. Table 1 includes Adam with epsilon 10^-3, Yogi, PAdam, PAMSGrad, AdaBound and AmsBound; Tables 2–3 include the latter four. These distinguish original Adam's deficit from adaptive variants that approach or exceed momentum. For example, Table 3 best accuracies are PAdam 77.51 ± 0.19, PAMSGrad 77.67 ± 0.14 and AdaBound 77.50 ± 0.29, against momentum 77.50 ± 0.25.

record.verdict_notes: Use only the supplied text. All CIFAR experiments, including CIFAR-100, are stated to have six repetitions; the record's uncertainty about CIFAR-100 repetition count is incorrect. Optimizers are training methods, not model subjects. The language-model curves are already declared in rows_left_out and therefore are not added to missing. No test-error advantage for original Adam on CIFAR-10 ResNet20 survives correction of the cited comparator.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmark method-specific results; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Original Adam on CIFAR-10 ResNet20, ResNet56 and DenseNet under the study's broader tuning protocol
relationships.reason: R2, R6 and R10 are below the corrected within-study momentum baselines by 1.05, 1.29 and 1.71 percentage points, respectively.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum over Adam on all three architectures despite broader tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Original Adam on CIFAR-100 VGGNet and ResNet18 at epoch 250 and best test performance
relationships.reason: R18, R20, R26 and R28 show lower accuracy than momentum, including best-performance deficits of 2.25 and 1.36 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum at the late checkpoint and best reported performance on both architectures, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Original Adam on CIFAR-100 VGGNet and ResNet18 at epochs 50 and 150
relationships.reason: R14, R16, R22 and R24 have higher mean accuracy than momentum before the later reversal; the relative performance depends on training stage.
relationships.display_finding: Reported early Adam accuracy advantages over momentum before a later reversal remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Original AMSGrad on CIFAR-10 and later-stage CIFAR-100
relationships.reason: Text and omitted table entries show AMSGrad below the study's momentum baseline on all three CIFAR-10 architectures and at epoch 250 and best performance on both CIFAR-100 architectures.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored momentum over AMSGrad across CIFAR-10 and later CIFAR-100 evaluations, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Existing modified adaptive methods on CIFAR-100 ResNet18 at best performance
relationships.reason: Omitted Table 3 entries show PAdam at 77.51%, PAMSGrad at 77.67% and AdaBound at 77.50%, versus momentum at 77.50%; the deficit does not extend uniformly across adaptive variants.
relationships.display_finding: Reported PAdam, PAMSGrad, and AdaBound performance near or above momentum remains unverified.
